module_title: Banking and Financial Awareness: Insurance Market and Terminology (Level 2: Intermediate)
introduction: This intermediate level covers the supreme regulatory body (IRDAI), the core principles that govern insurance contracts, and high-frequency exam terminologies like Bancassurance. This depth is vital for IBPS PO, SBI PO, and RBI Assistant exams.

core_concepts.title: IRDAI (Insurance Regulatory and Development Authority of India)
core_concepts.description: Just as the RBI regulates banks, IRDAI regulates the entire insurance and reinsurance industry in India. It was established in 1999 based on the recommendations of the 'Malhotra Committee'. Its headquarters is located in Hyderabad, Telangana.

core_concepts.title: Bancassurance
core_concepts.description: A favorite question in banking exams! When a bank ties up with an insurance company to sell the insurer's products to its own bank customers through its branch network, this partnership is called 'Bancassurance'.

core_concepts.title: 2 Vital Principles of Insurance
core_concepts.description:
1. Utmost Good Faith (Uberrimae Fidei): Both the insurer and the insured must transparently disclose all material facts to each other (e.g., hiding a pre-existing disease invalidates the policy).
2. Principle of Indemnity: Insurance is meant to compensate for the exact loss suffered, not to help the insured make a profit out of a tragedy.

important_entities.name: GIC Re (General Insurance Corporation of India)
important_entities.key_fact: The sole domestic 'Reinsurance' company in the Indian insurance market.
important_entities.significance: Reinsurance simply means 'insurance for insurance companies'. When primary insurers (like New India Assurance) take on massive risks (like insuring an airline), they buy a policy from GIC Re to protect themselves from bankruptcy in case of a huge claim.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.alert_title: Exception to the Principle of Indemnity
trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: A major trap in statement-based questions: 'Does the principle of indemnity apply to Life Insurance?' NO! Human life cannot be assigned a monetary value. Therefore, upon death, the full 'Sum Assured' is paid, not a calculated compensation for the 'financial loss' of the person.

mnemonics_and_tricks.memory_phrase: 'M' for Money (Banking) is Narasimham, 'M' for Mortality (Insurance) is Malhotra
mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Examiners love to swap the Narasimham Committee (Banking Reforms) with the R.N. Malhotra Committee (Insurance Reforms) to confuse candidates. Keep them distinct!

exam_strategy_tips: For PO-level exams, make sure you know the definitions of auxiliary terms like 'Rider' (an add-on benefit to a base policy) and 'Surrender Value' (the amount you get if you terminate a life insurance policy before maturity).
